Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by assigning sequential identifiers, stamping dates, routing forms through designated approval channels, and storing executed documents in a controlled archive with access logs.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared a disposal plan document naming a non-licensed site and a date-time window. The actor created a waste manifest document with altered fields in the processor-identification field and the waste-description field, replacing licensed values with falsified descriptors. The actor created a second manifest copy with a different date stamp. The actor drafted a communication message in a channel document addressed to a named account, describing the falsified manifest values and the site location.

3) Materials/access observed: One disposal plan document; two waste manifest documents with altered processor-identification, waste-description, and date fields; one communication message in a channel; access to a named account on that channel; the site location and date-time window stated in the plan document.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Sequential identifiers on the two manifests; mismatched processor-identification values between manifests; a date stamp on the second manifest differing from the first; a channel message referencing manifest identifiers that do not match a licensed-processor registry entry; the plan document's site field naming a non-licensed location.
